correctness.rationale: In the repaired statement the current diagonal rule means sequential size-biased removal. Exponential races have this law by the minimum and memorylessness identities, and conditional on the final heavy clock the light count is binomial. The unit-rate maximum has mean H_r and bounded variance by independent exponential spacings. Hence its clock induces a random binomial mean μ_n+O_P(1), because the remainder O_P((log r)²/n) goes to zero. In the conditional centered characteristic function the quadratic term tends to −t²/2 and the uniform cubic error O(mp_n|t|³/μ_n^(3/2)) vanishes in probability. Boundedness of characteristic functions permits mixing and the O_P(1) shift vanishes after scaling. The residual trace after r+s pivots with h heavy coordinates left is m−s+(a−1)h. At the prescribed window the strict inequality a−1>εm+s eventually holds, so success means L≤s. Rounding does not change the continuity limit. Monotonicity of residual trace gives the extended zero/one limits without requiring the exact event reduction outside the window. The retained finite identities follow by binomial expansion of the conditional mass and generating function, and the fixed-rank comparison follows by mixing the conditional Poisson limit over the exponential spacings.
residual_risks: The finite published checker supports the finite formulas, not the asymptotic theorem. No simulation or claim about finite-size Gaussian accuracy is used.
The boundary ε=λ is excluded and μ_n cannot in general be replaced by its leading equivalent at window precision.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem gives instance-specific operationally interpretable mathematical information not available from an expected-error bound: it resolves both the oversampling threshold and the probability across its transition. It separates the bounded heavy-clock fluctuations from Gaussian light-count fluctuations, explaining the scale and why a limit for the last heavy clock alone gives the wrong success window.
residual_risks: The value is the sharp transition for this diagonal test family, not evidence of similar performance on dense matrices or in floating point.
